description: Representative ATen schema (verbatim, representative and NOT exclusive): aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view_copy(Tensor self) -> Tensor. All supplied registered signatures: aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view_copy(Tensor self) -> Tensor ; aten::_test_autograd_multiple_dispatch_view_copy.out(Tensor self, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). This definition represents only the functional overload above; the original Gems pytest owns the full contract and defines the overloads, keyword arguments, return values, errors, aliasing and mutation semantics that must be supported. Do not narrow the tests to this single signature and do not adapt reference behavior to fit it. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator flattens self into a rank-1 contiguous copy whose stride is (1,); for non-empty results the test also asserts that the result storage pointer differs from the input's and that filling either operand leaves the other unchanged (the pointer check is skipped for zero-element operands, where both sides may hold nullptr storage); a lazy negation or conjugate bit on the source is materialized so the result reports is_neg() == False and is_conj() == False, and empty operands are supported. Only layouts admitting a flat view are accepted (contiguous, last-dim strided, narrow/uniform offsets, unsqueeze, fully zero-stride expansion); transposed, permuted, partially expanded and gap-sliced operands raise RuntimeError from the operator under test, the exception type being the only property the test asserts. The result is differentiable: backward produces a gradient on the operator's device. The original pytest additionally exercises the out= overload, which writes into a keyword-only buffer, returns that same buffer (identity), keeps non-contiguous view buffers within their surrounding storage, resizes a zero-element buffer, and raises for dtype-mismatched or non-tensor out. A non-tensor operand raises RuntimeError or TypeError; a missing operand raises RuntimeError.
